items.number: Provincial cost of raising a dollar relative to federal (excess burden ratio)
items.flips: national standard for the environment from 1.0; for schools from 1.5; provinces below that
items.status: unknown: the published range spans both sides of both thresholds
items.watch: A matched-year, same-method estimate of the marginal cost of public funds for federal and provincial income taxes. No scheduled release.

items.number: Saving from one national transit system over separate city or provincial systems
items.flips: national from about 10%; below that, provinces (or cities)
items.watch: Cost benchmarking of Canadian transit agencies by network size (for example the Canadian Urban Transit Association's annual fact book).

items.number: Share of transit benefit carried by commuters across the metro boundary
items.flips: cities beat provinces only near zero; by 10% provinces win
items.current: below 50% by construction of metro boundaries; not measured
items.status: unknown, but the census can measure it
items.watch: 2026 Census commuting-flow tables (place of residence by place of work), not yet scheduled.

items.number: Spread of emissions per person across provinces (log standard deviation)
items.flips: a carbon price beats a uniform quantity standard at any spread from 0.2

projected.2030: 0.67 with current measures, 0.64 with additional measures
projected.2035: 0.68 with current measures, 0.66 with additional measures

items.status: safe through 2035: projected spread stays about 3.4 times the threshold
items.watch: ECCC's annual emissions projections and National Inventory Report.

items.number: Weight on inequality (elasticity of marginal utility of income)
items.flips: a national floor provinces can top up starts to win from 2.0 (with low tax distortion)
items.watch: New estimates from happiness or willingness-to-pay studies.
